also.title: Emotional reunions with loved ones for Oleshky evacuees

explained.headline: Evacuees leave Russian-occupied Oleshky as regional ceasefire holds

happened.text: Evacuees were reunited with relatives at the border after years of separation and severe hardship, including food shortages and living without basic utilities.

background.text: Oleshky, located in the Kherson region near the front line, has been occupied by Russian forces since the full-scale invasion in February 2022.
The town's population plummeted from twenty-four thousand before the war to an estimated two thousand as supply deliveries stopped and escape routes became heavily mined.

matters.text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that the evacuation operation demonstrated that de-escalation steps with Russia are achievable under pressure.

terms.definition: An international forum for the governments of major industrialized and emerging economies to discuss global economic and geopolitical issues.

removed.text: Hundreds of civilians evacuated from the Russian-occupied southern Ukrainian town of Oleshky and crossed into Kyiv-controlled territory via Belarus following a localized ceasefire.
why: Evidence mentions hundreds but does not specify the number of civilians or the exact route.

why: The claim states the note as a fact rather than attributed to Rubio.

removed.text: Reports regarding a drone attack on an industrial facility and oil refinery near Moscow remain unverified independently.
why: Evidence mentions a drone attack near Kstovo, not Moscow.

removed.text: The exact timing and formal participation structure for upcoming peace negotiations involving Russia, Ukraine, and the United States remain subject to ongoing diplomatic discussion.
why: The claim is stated as fact; the evidence attributes it to a Kremlin aide.

sources.title: Thousands rally in New Delhi to demand India’s election chief resign
India news: Opposition holds major rally in Delhi over voter roll revisions
Indian forces tighten security in Delhi ahead of big opposition protest

explained.headline: Indian opposition protests voter list revisions and election chief

happened.text: Thousands of protesters and opposition leaders marched in New Delhi to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
Indian National Congress party leader Rahul Gandhi led the demonstration on Sunday following more than a month of protests challenging voter roll revisions.
Authorities deployed hundreds of police officers and riot-control vehicles while announcing traffic diversions ahead of the march toward Ramlila Maidan.

background.text: Opposition parties, student organisations and youth groups have staged near-daily demonstrations since late September calling for Kumar to step down.

matters.text: Opposition parties alleged the voter list revisions disproportionately removed Muslims and minorities unlikely to support Prime Minister Narendra Modi's party.
Analysts described the demonstrations and growing opposition support as Prime Minister Narendra Modi's most serious political crisis since taking office.
Health Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda characterized the demonstration as a calculated conspiracy to plunge the nation into anarchy.

uncertain.text: The Election Commission denied favouring any political party and stated that voters whose names were wrongly removed may register again.
The Bharatiya Janata Party accused opposition parties of attempting to undermine democracy by challenging legitimate electoral procedures.

terms.definition: An autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering election processes in India.
A historic large ground in New Delhi frequently used for public gatherings and political rallies.

removed.text: It remains unverified whether the voter roll purges targeted specific communities intentionally, as official bodies and opposition parties dispute the motivations.
why: interpretation attributes a view to someone

removed.text: The protests began after a voter verification exercise removed more than 130 million names from electoral rolls across the country.
why: The evidence states around 130 million, not an exact count of more than 130 million.

removed.text: Prime Minister Narendra Modi leads the governing Bharatiya Janata Party, whose Hindu nationalist platform has held power since 2014.
why: Evidence mentions Modi came to power in 2014, but does not explicitly state the party platform held power.
